newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Foreign shareholder cuts stake in Foshan.
newsitem.headline: Foreign shareholder cuts stake in Foshan.

text.p: Foshan Electrical and Lighting Co Ltd said on Friday that Arran Investment Pte Ltd, a Singapore company, had reduced its stake in the lightbulb maker by two percentage points to 8.64 percent.
Arran Investment sold Foshan's B shares, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, between December 9, 1996, and April 22, Foshan said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Before December 9, Arran held 29.36 million B shares and by April 22 it had 23.84 million, the statement said.
A Foshan spokesman said Arran's sale was due to profit-taking and did not reflect any loss of confidence in the company.
Trading in Foshan's A and B shares was suspended on Friday morning for the announcement and will resume in the afternoon, according to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
On Thursday, the company's B shares closed at HK$7.80 and the A shares ended at 16.36 yuan.

At the end of 1996, Arran held 26.81 million B shares, or 9.72 percent, of Foshan's 275.86 million outstanding shares, making it the second biggest shareholder, according to the company's 1996 annual report.
Foshan posted net profits of 193.11 million yuan for 1996 against 170.24 milion for 1995 based on international accounting standards.
